alt: A document detailing the DAST-10 (Drug Abuse Screening Test) questionnaire and its interpretation guidelines.
summary:
This document introduces and outlines the DAST-10 (Drug Abuse Screening Test), a 10-item brief screening tool designed to assess drug use over the past 12 months, explicitly excluding alcohol and tobacco. It can be administered by a clinician or self-administered, requiring yes/no responses and typically completed in under 8 minutes. The document provides a clear definition of "drug abuse" for the purpose of the test, encompassing non-medical use of drugs and use of prescribed/OTC medications in excess of directions, listing various classes of drugs covered.

The legal significance of the DAST-10 lies in its utility as a standardized, quantifiable screening instrument for drug abuse, which can be critical in various legal and forensic contexts. Results from this tool can inform substance abuse evaluations for court proceedings, probation, parole, child custody cases, or professional fitness assessments. The clear scope (excluding alcohol/tobacco) and structured scoring provide a consistent framework for assessing drug-related problems, which can support legal decisions regarding treatment, intervention, or risk assessment. The suggested actions based on scores offer a pathway for clinical and potentially legally mandated follow-up.

No significant discrepancies are observed within the document. It consistently defines the DAST-10's purpose, scope, and administration. The scoring mechanism is clearly articulated, including the specific exception for question #3 where a "no" response yields a point. The interpretation table directly correlates scores with degrees of problems and suggested actions, maintaining internal consistency. A reference for the DAST-10's origin is also provided, enhancing its credibility.

DAST-10
Introduction
The Drug Abuse Screening Test (DAST-10) is a 10-item brief screening tool
that can be administered by a clinician or self-administered. Each question
requires a yes or no response, and the tool can be completed in less than 8
minutes. This tool assesses drug use, not including alcohol or tobacco use,
in the past 12 months.
http://www.drugabuse.gov/nidamed-medical-health-professionals
DAST-10 Questionnaire
I'm going to read you a list of questions concerning information about your potential involvement with
drugs, excluding alcohol and tobacco, during the past 12 months.
When the words "drug abuse" are used, they mean the use of prescribed or over-the-counter
medications/drugs in excess of the directions and any non-medical use of drugs. The various classes of
drugs may include: cannabis (e.g., marijuana, hash), solvents, tranquilizers (e.g., Valium), barbiturates,
cocaine, stimulants (e.g., speed), hallucinogens (e.g., LSD) or narcotics (e.g., heroin). Remember that the
questions do not include alcohol or tobacco.
If you have difficulty with a statement, then choose the response that is mostly right.
You may choose to answer or not answer any of the questions in this section.
These questions refer to the past 12 months.

Interpreting the DAST 10
In these statements, the term "drug abuse" refers to the use of medications at a level that exceeds the
instructions, and/or any non-medical use of drugs. Patients receive 1 point for every "yes" answer with
the exception of question #3, for which a "no" answer receives 1 point. DAST-10 Score Degree of
